Why E-Ink Is Easier on the Eyes

By Ada Lovelace · March 14, 2025

Electronic paper does not shine light into your eyes. Instead, it reflects the light around you, just like a printed page. That single difference explains most of why an hour with an e-reader feels so unlike an hour with a phone or a laptop.

How the display works

Each pixel of an E Ink panel holds millions of tiny capsules filled with black and white particles. A small electric charge pulls one colour to the surface and pushes the other down. Once the particles have moved, they stay put without using any power, which is why the screen can show a page for weeks on a single charge.

Because the image is made of real pigment rather than light, the contrast looks the same in bright sunlight as it does under a reading lamp. Glossy screens wash out outdoors; paper-like screens get easier to read.

What it means for reading

Researchers who compared reading on paper, e-ink and backlit tablets found that comprehension on e-ink was close to paper for long, linear texts. The differences grew for tasks that needed flipping back and forth, where physical pages still win.

The best screen for a novel is the one you forget you are looking at.

There are trade-offs. Page turns are slower, colour is limited or absent, and images can look muddy. For articles and books, though, the calm, steady page is hard to beat & well worth the compromises.

  • No backlight shining at your eyes
  • Readable in direct sunlight
  • Weeks of battery life
